small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs targeting the M=16384, N=4096, K=4096 shape: BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=32 with num_warps=8, num_stages=4, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32 num_warps=8 num_stages=4. Drop tiny tiles (64x128, 128x64) since M,N,K are all multiples of 128 — masks become dead code if you assert divisibility.
- Since M,N,K are all multiples of the largest tile, generate a no-mask fast path (or use `EVEN_K: tl.constexpr` flag) to remove per-iter K masking in the inner loop; this often gives ~10–15% on big GEMMs.
- Cache `WT` and the folded `scale`/`shift` once on the module (not recomputed per forward), and ensure they live as contiguous fp32 to avoid stride-1 misses.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a split-K or stream-K GEMM: at M=16384, N=4096, K=4096 the workload is 64 tiles × 32 tiles = 2048 CTAs which already saturates the 4090, but stream-K gives better tail balance and consistently beats cuBLAS by a few percent on Ada. Persist programs and use atomics only when split factor > 1.
- Store B (weight) in a pre-swizzled / pre-transposed layout once at init (already partially done), and consider keeping A in fp32 but using TF32 `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` — the reference `nn.Linear` uses cuBLAS which on Ada may use TF32 by default; matching that lets you halve K-loop traffic per dot.
- Fuse the BN affine + GELU·ReLU epilogue exactly as today, but compute it on the accumulator before writeback (already done) — no further fusion exists; the gap to baseline is purely GEMM throughput, so the redesign should focus on matching cuBLAS-class GEMM (stream-K + TF32 + vectorized 128-bit loads).
